Ensemble drift detector (CEDD and FEDD)

Source: R/dfr_ensemble.R
dfr_ensemble.Rd

Combines the detections of several drift detectors by voting (Giusti Tavares et al., 2025). At every time step the vote is the sum of the members' scores, and the ensemble reports a drift when the vote passes the voting rule:

  • "efer" (early find, early report): vote >= 1;

  • "majority": vote > n / 2 (n members);

  • "threshold": vote >= threshold.

With tolerance k <= 1 the scores are crisp: 1 when the member detects a drift at that time step, 0 otherwise (crisp ensemble drift detector, CEDD). With k > 1 they are fuzzy (fuzzy ensemble drift detector, FEDD). A detection at time d gives time t the score 1 - |t - d| / k when |t - d| < k. A member's score is the largest over its detections. So detections that are close in time but not simultaneous can still add up to a majority.

Usage

dfr_ensemble(
  drifter_list,
  voting = c("majority", "efer", "threshold"),
  threshold = NULL,
  tolerance = 0,
  lookahead = TRUE
)

Arguments

drifter_list

Named list of drifters (dist_based or mv_dist_based) run in parallel on the stream.

voting

Voting rule: "majority" (default), "efer" or "threshold".

threshold

Vote needed by the "threshold" rule (lambda).

tolerance

Time tolerance k of the fuzzy scores; 0 (default) gives the crisp ensemble.

lookahead

With fuzzy scores, TRUE (default) uses detections on both sides of a time step, as in the paper. The vote of time t is then known only when t + k - 1 has arrived, so drifts are reported k - 1 observations after the time they refer to (obj$events holds those times). FALSE uses only the detections up to the current observation and reports at once.

Value

dfr_ensemble object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, on every observation, the decision of each member, the time step whose vote was decided (time) and the vote (vote). obj$events holds the time steps of the ensemble drifts, including those decided when the stream ended.

Details

The combination follows the reference code (https://github.com/cefet-rj-dal/reproduce, fedd/core/4-ensemble-fuzzy.R, with the triangular fuzzification of harbinger):

  • The majority rule is strict, vote > n / 2 (the paper writes vote >= the ceiling of n / 2).

  • After a fuzzy ensemble drift at time t, the detections before t are forgotten. Each member with a positive score at t also loses its first detection at or after t, or its next detection if none has arrived yet. So one detection does not raise a second ensemble drift.

  • The scores are (k - j) * (1 / k) at distance j, as in harbinger. The paper's Equation 3 prints |t - t'| / k, which would give 0 at the detection itself.

Members with a target_feat receive that column of each row, the other univariate members the row mean, and multivariate members the row (as dfr_multi_criteria()). The members are not reset by the ensemble. The paper's members are also run as separate detectors, each with its own warm-up and normalisation, before the vote.

ensemble_vote() applies the same voting to detection series computed beforehand.

References

Giusti Tavares, L., Lima, J., Melo, M., Chen, C., Garibaldi, J., Scatena, G. S., Costa, A. H. R., Gomi, E. S., Salles, R., Pacitti, E., Santos, I., Siqueira, I. G., Carvalho, D., Coutinho, R., Porto, F. and Ogasawara, E. (2025). Fuzzy-based ensemble method for robust concept drift detection in multivariate time series. 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN). doi:10.1109/IJCNN64981.2025.11228919

See also

ensemble_vote(), dfr_multi_criteria().

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
data <- data.frame(serie = c(stats::rnorm(500), stats::rnorm(500, 3)))
members <- list(ph = dfr_page_hinkley(), kswin = dfr_kswin(), adwin = dfr_adwin())
# Crisp majority: the members must agree on the same observation.
crisp <- fit(dfr_ensemble(members, voting = "majority"), data)
crisp$events
#> integer(0)
# Fuzzy majority with a tolerance of 50 observations.
fuzzy <- fit(dfr_ensemble(members, voting = "majority", tolerance = 50), data)
fuzzy$events
#> [1] 507
